CheckTitle: Vercel projects run a supported Node.js version
Description: This check reports projects pinned to a Node.js version that has reached end of life and therefore no longer receives security patches from either the Node.js project or Vercel.
Risk: An end-of-life runtime accumulates **unpatched vulnerabilities in the JavaScript engine and the standard library**, including HTTP request parsing and TLS handling that process untrusted input on every request. Because the runtime sits underneath the application, no amount of application-level review addresses those flaws, and Vercel eventually stops building projects pinned to retired versions.

Code.Other:
1. Open the project in the Vercel dashboard
2. Go to **Settings > General > Node.js Version**
3. Select the current LTS release
4. Update the `engines.node` field in `package.json` to match, so local and CI builds agree
5. Run the test suite against the new version before promoting to production
6. Deploy to a preview environment first and confirm behaviour, particularly around any native dependencies

Recommendation.Text: Move projects to the current Node.js LTS release, align the engines field in package.json, and validate on a preview deployment before promoting.
